id: ISS-0950
title: "Catalog service endpoint_url is not URL-validated at registration/publish time (decision 0027 gap)"
discovered_by: SECURITY-REVIEWER
discovered_in_run: WF03-ISS0917-20261001 (filed by ORCH)

severity: MINOR
owner: "ELIXIR-DEV"
description: >
  Found by SECURITY-REVIEWER in WF03-ISS0917-20261001. POST /service-catalog and publish do no
  UrlValidator check on endpoint_url; the only control is the dispatch-time INV-9 gate in
  ServiceTaskDispatcher.http_transport/3. ISS-0917's fix makes catalog endpoints reachable by the
  dispatcher for the first time, so add fast-feedback syntactic validation (https scheme, host not
  private/loopback literal) at register/publish time in Letflow.ServiceCatalog /
  Routers.AdminServices. Defense in depth; dispatch gate stays binding. Severity MINOR (hardening).
  Owner ELIXIR-DEV (via CODE-DESIGNER).

  - lib/letflow/routers/admin_services.ex

task.description: WF-03 Step 3d REVIEWER gate. Review the implementation on branch feature/WF03-ISS0950-20261001 (git diff origin/main...HEAD -- lib/ test/) for idiomatic Elixir/Ecto, scope creep (only what the validated design lib/letflow/design/iss0950-catalog-endpoint-url-register-validation.md requires), decision-record consistency (0027, and anything on UrlValidator/INV-9), no supervision-tree impact, correct @spec/@doc, no duplicated blocklist, validate/1,2 behaviour unchanged. Look specifically at SECURITY-REVIEWER's MINOR 3 (validate(url, :no_dns) now returns :ok for hostnames -- a public footgun on the existing function; decide whether it needs a guard so only validate_syntactic/1 reaches the :no_dns branch, and if you rate it MAJOR say how, otherwise MINOR). Read handoffs/WF03-ISS0950-20261001/step-03-elixir-dev.json and step-03c-security-reviewer.json. Complete PASS/FAIL per HANDOFF_PROTOCOL.md (set status COMPLETED and write the result block yourself). Do not commit; leave lib/ test/ web/ unmodified.
acceptance_criteria: Idiom, scope-creep, decision-consistency each answered with file:line evidence

result.summary: REVIEWER verdict PASS. Idiom: check_endpoint_url/1 (entry.ex:~258) uses with/else, binary matching, pure no-DNS; validate_endpoint_url/1 private changeset helper uses get_field so an inherited stored URL on publish is checked, skips nil and already-errored (no duplicate); wired into both changesets (entry.ex:156, 219). Has @spec/@doc/@moduledoc paragraph. Scope: only entry.ex, service_catalog.ex (doc-only), url_validator.ex, one test seeded as legacy data; router untouched as the design specifies (changeset clause already exists admin_services.ex:235/263/314); no new behaviour/macro/plumbing. Decisions: 0027 consistent (dispatch INV-9 gate stays binding, advisory only); blocklist not duplicated (validate_syntactic reuses check_ip_literal via check_host); validate/1,2 behaviour unchanged for function resolvers; no supervision-tree impact (pure functions, no process). No new type-safety gap requiring an issue beyond MINOR-3 below.

issues.description: SECURITY MINOR-3 disposition: rated MINOR, not MAJOR. url_validator.ex:129 `:not_an_ip when dns_resolver == :no_dns -> :ok` is reachable via public validate/2 (url_validator.ex:48-55) with the literal atom :no_dns, which validate/2's @spec (dns_resolver() = function) excludes, so Dialyzer flags any such caller; no caller passes it (grep: only url_validator.ex:70); previously a non-function crashed (fail-closed), now fails open for hostnames only (IP-literal blocklist and scheme still enforced). Not exploitable: needs a deliberate atom, and the dispatch gate calls validate with a real resolver. Recommended optional hardening for a follow-up (ELIXIR-DEV, type-safety): add `when is_function(dns_resolver, 1)` to validate/2, or route validate_syntactic through a private check_host_syntactic/1 so :no_dns never enters check_host's resolver parameter and the widened private @spec union goes away. Not blocking.

Design doc says no router change; affected_files in ISS-0950 lists routers/admin_services.ex. Consistent with design (changeset clauses already exist); noted only so TEST-DESIGNER covers the HTTP 422 path as the design's router-level assertions require.
Pre-existing shared-blocklist gaps (0.0.0.0/8, 100.64.0.0/10, multicast) already recorded by SECURITY-REVIEWER and the design; not for this change.
